The test's copy is the problem, not the count: because the assertion's expected value is produced by the same expression as the value under test, the assertion is a duplicate of the implementation rather than an independent statement about it. This is the mechanism behind the r7 blocker -- see that finding.

RenderReportTests._write_calls() (tests/test_code_map.py:145-151) reaches into supplement.json and re-derives the renderer's write count as `1 + len(supp['modules']) + len(supp['entities'])`. That arithmetic is render.run()'s, hand-copied into the test. It is only correct while every supplement entity is reachable through `children`; nothing checks that, so a future extractor change makes the input precondition overstate silently and the guard stops guarding. Observation-grade -- it holds today, measured: 1 + 112 + 3536 = 3649 against 3648 files on disk.

Two prose blocks in the delta assert more than the code delivers, and in this issue that is not a style point. After the fix the number cannot be wrong -- mutation N8 deletes every second entity page after writing and all 17 tests stay green. The docstring states the test's falsifying power in exactly the terms this issue exists to police, and overstates it. (2) tests/test_code_map.py:180-184 asserts 'A blunt scan of the REAL page tree still reports two hits'; a fresh build at HEAD returns three, the third being that docstring itself. Both are load-bearing rationale, not decoration -- (1) is why the test looks sufficient and (2) is why the fixture is synthetic. Escalated to the r7 blocker.
